name: Atmospheric CO₂
summary: CO₂ 428.6 ppm at Mauna Loa in the week of 8 Nov, up 2.34 ppm on a year, inside the 2–3 ppm Watch band
state: Mauna Loa recorded 428.64 ppm in the week of 8 Nov, 2.34 ppm higher than a year earlier, inside the 2.0–3.0 ppm Watch band (NOAA GML). The previous week's reading showed growth of 3.36 ppm, above the Alert line, so the level falls back to Watch. Weekly growth figures are noisy, and El Niño years tend to bring faster CO₂ growth as tropical land absorbs less carbon.
for_you: CO₂ growth has no immediate local effect; it sets the pace of long-run warming. Readers can follow official climate assessments for context.
rubric_hit: CO₂ y/y +2.34 ppm within 2.0–3.0 ppm Watch band

why: CO₂ concentration is the main long-run driver of warming; the growth rate shows whether emissions cuts are biting.
drivers: Fossil emissions, land sinks, El Niño (weakens sinks), wildfires.
